newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Latam,basic banking boost Spain's BBV.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Latam,basic banking boost Spain's BBV.

text.p: Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya said on Thursday its first-quarter earnings rose nearly 25 percent, bolstered by strong gains in its Latin American business and strength in traditional banking.
BBV said its attributable profit rose 24.8 percent in the first quarter to 24.73 billion pesetas ($169.8 million) in line with analysts' average forecasts of a 24.2 percent gain.
"The results reflect the success of our 1,000 day plan to reinforce our domestic position, which has been very good, and to export our know-how to Latin America," a top BBV official told Reuters.
A Latin American shopping spree in recent months has put a strong shine on earnings, as analysts expected.
BBV recently acquired the branch networks of Banca Cremi and Banco de Oriente in Mexico and also purchased Colombia's leading bank Banco Ganadero as well as Banco Frances del Rio de la Plata.
Pre-tax profits from BBV's Latin American groups were 10.45 billion pesetas in the first quarter, compared with total pre-tax profit of 57.77 billion pesetas, BBV said in a statement.

Excluding Latin American holdings, the bank's ordinary margin, which reflects loan, commission and own-account trading earnings, would have risen 11 percent instead of the 33.8 percent jump it registered overall, the BBV official said.

"The results were very good," said Juan Cueto, analyst at Ibersecurities in Madrid. "There is a great potential in Latin America with the reduction of general expenses, personnel expenses, etc and in productivity improvement."
The bank expected strong further gains in Latin America, adding that its earnings could weather a problem in the region without difficulty, the official said.
Were things to go wrong, BBV could write-off its Latin American holdings -- worth about the same as half its industrial portfolio -- without imperilling its earnings or dividend.
"We are very positive about the change of trend in Latin America, sociologically, politically and economically. We think it is stable and lasting," he said.
But the bank and analysts were quick to note that domestic business had also performed well, as the economy grew, financial markets rose and margins held firm despite a tough competitive environment.

"The results were very good. They had strong growth in almost all categories," another Madrid-based analyst said. "There was the Latin American factor and, also, the domestic business...Margins were stable and volumes increased."
"Our business, in terms of both volumes and margins has gone very well," the BBV source said. "Investment funds continue to evolve favourably and commissions were strong." ($ = 145.6 Spanish Pesetas)
